title: Time-and-Materials Project Time Drawn from TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours
content:
**Scope.** This rule governs a group of time-and-materials project time drawn from a TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours block that is the TimeBank route of exactly one time-and-materials statement of work, meaning the client holds exactly one time-and-materials engagement whose status is signed, in progress, on hold or pending acceptance, a group being the block-routed lines of that statement of work for one date and level. For such a group, and only for such a group, the group is drawn for the summed logged minutes of its lines, which the statement of work already logs in billing-increment steps for every block size that may draw project work, and the block hours are figured under the project-time pricing. The project time of a client holding no such engagement or two or more of them keeps, wholly and line by line, the standard minutes rule, its recorded minutes rounded up to the billing increment, the standard conversion and the standard time band; a remote session, a service visit, an installation visit and a travel entry keep their own rules.

Whether a block's project time falls under this rule is decided by the client's engagement records alone, never by a timesheet line, so it does not change with what any engagement logs or with the order of drawing; inside that scope every group is priced from its own lines and the one statement of work alone, whatever order its lines were logged or drawn in.

**Band recorded.** For such a group the band recorded is holiday for a group dated on a Saturday or Sunday, after-hours for a weekday group with minutes logged in the after-hours band, and business hours otherwise, project work being scheduled and never an emergency, and a weekday observed holiday taking the band its lines are logged in. The draw is recorded with the minutes the group is drawn for as its worked minutes.

## Drawing a project group: `post_project_time_draw_e9603a55`

**Capability.** Draws the block hours of one group of time-and-materials project time from a TimeBank block, a group being the logged lines of one statement of work, work date and level: one project-work draw is added to the block's hours ledger for the given statement of work, work date and level, and the block's remaining hours go down by the hours drawn. The client sees the project draw on the block's hours statement and the lower remaining balance.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `timebank_block_id` | Reference number of the TimeBank block the project time is drawn from, as returned by the TimeBank block lookup. |
| `sow_number` | The statement of work the time was logged under, SOW- followed by 6 digits, as shown on the project time log. |
| `entry_date` | The date the time was worked, YYYY-MM-DD, US Eastern calendar date. |
| `time_band` | The band the draw is recorded in: `business_hours` records a draw priced at a multiplier of one; `after_hours` records a draw priced at the block's after-hours multiplier; `emergency` records an emergency call-out priced with the block's emergency multiplier; `holiday` records weekend or holiday work priced at the block's holiday multiplier; `not_applicable` is never used for a work draw and is listed only because the ledger carries it for other entries. |
| `resource_level` | The level of the group drawn: `technician` records a draw at the technician ratio; `senior_engineer` at the senior engineer ratio; `architect` at the solutions architect ratio; `not_applicable` is never used for a work draw. |
| `worked_minutes` | The minutes the group is drawn for, after any floor or whole-hour rounding the rule applies, integer minutes. |
| `hours` | The block hours the group draws, 2 decimal places, rounded half up before it is passed. |

**Return.** `ledger_entry_reference` (reference of the new draw), `block_reference` (the block drawn from), `sow_number`, `entry_date`, `hours` and `hours_balance_after` (the block's remaining hours after the draw, 2 decimal places). The `ledger_entry_reference` confirms the draw.
